p:cNvPr.descr: PART 1: An image of citrate synthase. From top left, His320 is the left point of a pentagon, which has a double bond on the side going right and down. H over N is the second point (clockwise), and N bonds to H at the fourth point. To the right of that is the oxaloacetate chain, where O double bonds right to C, which bonds right to COO- and bonds down to H2C, which bonds right to COO-. To the right of that is the acetyl-CoA chain. It begins with a pentagon at the top, where the left point has a double bond on the side going up and right. There is 1+ at this point on the inside of the pentagon. H over N is at the second point, and His274 is at the third point. A double bond is on the right side going down, and N is at the fifth point. N bonds down to H. There is a red curved arrow pointing from H up to N. Below that is a chain starting H over HC bonding down to H and right to C, which double bonds up to O (all in pink). C bonds right to S-CoA. There is a red arrow from the red H to the red C. Below this is O double bonding down and right, then up and right to O. These both bond down to Asp375. An arrow points down from these chains to another set of chains. To the left of the arrow is step 1: The thioester linkage in acetyl-CoA activates the methyl hydrogens. Asp375 abstracts a proton from the methyl group, forming an enolate intermediate. The intermediate is stabilized by hydrogen bonding to and/or protonation by His274 (full protonation is shown). The next chain, from the left is a pentagon with His320 on the left point. H over N is at the second point. There is a double bond on the bottom left side of the pentagon. N is at the fourth point, which bonds to H. There is a red curved arrow pointing from the bonding mark back to N. To the right of this is O double bonding to C, which bonds right to COO- and down to H2C, which bonds right to COO-. There is a curved red arrow from this chain pointing back to H. To the right of this, a pentagon is at the top with nothing on the left point. There is a double bond on the bottom left and right sides of the pentagon. At the second point is H over N. The third point is His274, and the fifth point is N. Below N are two small red dots, then three blue lines, the H. There is a curved red arrow pointing from the two red dots to H. H bonds down and right to O (pink), which bonds down to C (pink), which double bonds left to H over HC (pink) and bonds right to S-CoA. There is a curved red arrow from the bonding line between H and O (pink) that points to the bonding line between the pink O and C. There is also a curved arrow from the H over HC double bond line to C (in pink) that points back to C in the previous chain. Below this, It is identified as Enol intermediate. Below this is H bonding down to O, which bonds down and left, then double bonds up and left to O. Both bonds down to Asp375. A black arrow points down to the next chain. To the left of the arrow is the following explanation: The enol(ate) rearranges to attack the carbonyl carbon of oxaloacetate, with His274 positioned to abstract the proton it had previously donated. His 320 acts as a general acid. The resulting condensation generates citroyl-CoA. The next diagram below this begins on the left with a pentagon. The left point is His320. The second point is H over N, and the fourth point is N (with two small red dots to the right). There is a double bond on the bottom left and right sides of the pentagon. To the right of this is another chain, identified as citroyl-CoA. It begins at the top with a pentagon. Inside the pentagon at the first point on the left there is a dashed curved line with a plus sign. H over N is the second point, His274 is the third point, and N over H is the fifth point. There are three blue lines below and left of H, then O, which double bonds down to C and left to H over HC (all in pink). C also bonds right to S-CoA. H over HC bonds down to C, which bonds left to HO, right to COO-, and down to H2C, which bonds right to COO-. Below this is Asp375 with a bonding line down. Moving right, there is an arrow pointing right. This arrow has a curved arrow from H2O (where O is in blue) pointing up to CoA-SH. The step 3 explanation is: The thioester is subsequently hydrolyzed, regenerating CoA-SH and producing citrate. To the right of the arrow is --His320, which is also left of a white oval where the citrate chain is located. Moving right, the citrate chain begins with H over HC bonding right to COO- (where CO is pink and O is blue). H over HC bonds down to C, which bonds left to HO, right to COO-, and down to H2C, which bonds right to COO-. Below the white oval is ASP375 with the bonding line below it. Above the white oval is a bonding line on top of His274.
